definition: An ORM scores only the final answer; a PRM scores each intermediate reasoning step.
details: An ORM scores only the final answer; a PRM scores each intermediate reasoning step. PRMs give denser signal and better-guided search but are expensive to label and can be gamed by plausible-looking steps.

explainer.lead: An outcome reward model scores only the final answer, while a process reward model scores each intermediate reasoning step. It matters because denser step-level signal can guide reasoning search.

tiers.eli5: One grader only checks your final answer; the other grades every step of your work.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use PRMs to guide search over reasoning traces, gaining denser feedback; pitfalls are costly step-level labeling and gaming by steps that look plausible but are wrong.
tiers.paperLevel: ORM gives reward on the final answer only; PRM gives a reward per reasoning step, trading label cost and susceptibility to plausible-step gaming for denser guidance.

explainer.example: On a math problem, a PRM flags a flawed middle step that an ORM would ignore because the final answer happens to be correct.
